input_theorem: For a q^2+1 point candidate in GQ(q,q), the defect d satisfies A_line d=(q-1)d; at q=5 and delta=7 the shell bound forces d to be plus/minus one valued with seven entries of each sign.
support_requirement: Each seven-line sign support would induce minimum intersection degree at least 4.
gq_lemma: No seven lines in GQ(5,5) induce minimum intersection degree at least 4.

case_analysis.r=0: All six lines besides ell meet ell. Every intersection-point part has size at least 4 and totals 6, forcing one part of size 6; with ell this would be a seven-line pencil, but a GQ(5,5) pencil has exactly 6 lines.
case_analysis.r=1: The five lines meeting ell must form one part of size 5. Together with ell they form the full six-line pencil; the one line disjoint from ell meets at most one pencil line, so its induced degree is at most 1.
case_analysis.r=2: The four lines meeting ell have partition 4 or 2+2. In the first case a disjoint line has degree at most 2; in the second at most 3.

boundary: The argument excludes deficiency seven. It does not prove that deficiency eight is attainable; the upper bound 12 remains the existing explicit feasible witness.
